newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finmin plans PLN 9.6 bln 1998 gap - paper.
newsitem.headline: Polish finmin plans PLN 9.6 bln 1998 gap - paper.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry has planned 1998 budget spending at 142.9 billion zlotys and revenues at 133.3 billion zlotys, the daily Rzeczpospolita said on Wednesday.
The report confirmed the government's earlier statement that the ensuing deficit would be equivalent to 1.9 percent of gross domestic product compared with 2.8 percent planned for 1997.
Spending would be 12 percent higher in nominal terms than this year and revenues 15.3 percent higher.
On Tuesday the government postponed to Thursday talks on the 1998 budget draft after some ministers asked for more time to study finance ministry materials.
Government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska on Tuesday disclosed only the proposed budget deficit level and said other figures would be released on Thursday.
The paper, without naming sources, said that under the finance ministry's proposal banks are to finance 5.9 billion zlotys of the deficit and the non-banking sector the remainder.
Revenues from privatisation have been set at 6.5 billion zlotys next year compared with 4.5 billion zlotys in 1997.

The report confirmed the finance ministry's earlier statement that it wanted the budget to assume 9.5 percent year-on-year inflation in December next year compared with 14.6 percent in May and maintaining GDP growth at 5.5 percent.

The ministry also proposes that the budget assume export growth at 13.5 percent and import growth at 16.3 percent. The current account deficit is planned to increase to seven percent of GDP from the five percent forecast for 1997.
Rzeczpospolita said the finance ministry planned no tax changes next year.
